report:
**Conclusion:** Yes, denosumab (Prolia) significantly reduces the risk of vertebral fractures in patients with osteoporosis.

### Evidence Behind the Conclusion

1. **Mechanism of Action:**  
Denosumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody that targets and inhibits RANKL (receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand). By blocking RANKL from binding to its receptor on osteoclasts, denosumab suppresses osteoclast formation, function, and survival. This action decreases bone resorption, increases bone mineral density (BMD), and preserves structural integrity (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/cell-and-developmental-biology/articles/10.3389/fcell.2020.00325/full).

2. **Pivotal Clinical Trial Evidence (FREEDOM Trial):**  
The primary clinical evidence comes from the landmark, 3-year FREEDOM trial published in *The New England Journal of Medicine*. In this randomized controlled trial of postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, subcutaneous denosumab (60 mg every 6 months) significantly reduced the cumulative 3-year incidence of new radiographic vertebral fractures from **7.2% in the placebo group to 2.3% in the denosumab group**. This represents a **relative risk reduction of approximately 68%** (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa0809493).

3. **Broader Clinical Efficacy:**  
Systematic reviews and evidence-based summaries confirm that denosumab consistently lowers the risk of vertebral, nonvertebral, and hip fractures in osteoporotic patients (https://www.aafp.org/afp/2019/0501/od1). Because of these robust clinical trial results, major medical guidelines endorse denosumab as a key first-line antiresorptive treatment for individuals at high risk of osteoporotic fractures.
